title: Power Pages: site analytics and server logging configuration
notes: 2026-11-16: taken offline; the grace for pages published before the check existed is off
summary: Hold: the briefing incorrectly says the roadmap describes a tenant-wide policy and that all documented controls are per-site and portal-only. Microsoft documents automation for site settings, while the claimed administrator-only opt-in default is not established by the roadmap or Learn.

claims.claim: Roadmap item 578071 concerns Power Pages site analytics and server logging configuration.
claims.quote: "id": 578071; "title": "Power Pages: Administration and governance - Configure site analytics and server logging"

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.claim: The roadmap lists February CY2027 for general availability.

claims.claim: The roadmap lists October CY2026 for preview.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans integrated telemetry and analytics for Power Pages sites.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The planned Application Insights integration monitors site page views.
claims.quote: Use Application Insights to monitor page views, form interactions, session details, and client-side analytics.

claims.claim: The planned integration monitors form interactions.
claims.quote: Use Application Insights to monitor page views, form interactions, session details, and client-side analytics.

claims.claim: The planned integration monitors session details.
claims.quote: Track page views, form interactions, and session details using client-side analytics.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes client-side analytics of site traffic and user interactions.
claims.quote: You can monitor your Power Pages site traffic and user interactions with ease.

claims.claim: The planned feature detects server-side errors.
claims.quote: Detect server-side errors, performance issues, and access logs to resolve problems and optimize your site.

claims.claim: The planned feature helps identify performance issues.
claims.quote: Detect server-side errors, performance issues, and access logs to resolve problems and optimize your site.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes access logs and detailed server-side logging.
claims.quote: Gain insights into server-side errors and access detailed logs to quickly resolve issues and enhance site performance.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The roadmap says makers configure site analytics by opening the setup workspace and adding the analytics provider script.
claims.quote: To configure site analytics, makers must open the setup workspace and add the analytics provider script to enable traffic analytics.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes enablement by admins, makers or marketers for end users.
claims.quote: Enabled by admins/makers/marketers for end users

claims.claim: The new feature is admin-opt-in, requiring administrator enablement before anyone can use it.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages Application Insights site analytics server logging tenant policy enable disable licensing; "Power Pages" "site analytics" "Application Insights". Read roadmap, DevTools, telemetry-monitoring and analytics pages; none requires a separate admin enablement.
claims.fix: Change defaultState to user-opt-in: the roadmap says makers add the provider script, and the targeted searches found no separate administrator switch for this capability. Explain that this is maker-selected enablement, not a documented tenant admin gate.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model, licensing.notes, cost; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Application Insights introduces consumption billing, supporting the consumption licensing model and variable cost rating.
claims.quote: Application Insights is billed through the Log Analytics workspace into which its log data ingested.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/app/application-insights-faq to sources and cite it for the Azure meter; distinguish that published meter from unpublished feature-specific Power Pages licensing.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Feature-specific Power Pages licensing and charges have not yet been published.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Pages" "Application Insights" "license"; Power Pages Application Insights site analytics server logging tenant policy enable disable licensing. Read FAQ and licensing search excerpts, roadmap and telemetry-monitoring; no feature-specific terms found.

claims.claim: Application Insights billing depends on ingested telemetry volume.
claims.quote: Azure Application Insights is billed based on the volume of telemetry data your application sends (data ingestion) and how long time you want data to be available (data retention).
claims.fix: Cite this published Application Insights billing explanation or the Azure Monitor pricing documentation it links to; the existing Power Pages sources do not establish the ingestion meter.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: diagnostic logs row
claims.claim: Site diagnostic logging to Azure Blob storage is reached in Power Platform admin center through Resources > Power Pages sites > site > Site Actions > Enable diagnostics logs.
claims.quote: Under the Resources section, select Power Pages sites. ... Select your website. ... From the Site Actions menu, select Enable diagnostics logs.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: diagnostic logs row
claims.claim: An API or automation equivalent for enabling site diagnostic logs to Azure Blob storage is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages enable diagnostic logs Azure Blob storage API PowerShell CLI; "Power Pages" "diagnostic" "logging" "API". Opened view-portal-error-log and REST Power Platform Websites operations; no diagnostic-logging enable operation found.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls: site traffic analytics row
claims.claim: The new Power Platform admin center exposes tenant site traffic analytics through Manage > Products > Power Pages > Analytics (preview).
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select Manage. ... Under Products, select Power Pages and then select Analytics (preview).

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls: site traffic analytics row
claims.claim: The dashboard requires Dynamics 365 administrator, Power Platform administrator, or System administrator with visibility limited to their environments.
claims.quote: Dynamics 365 administrator; Power Platform administrator; System administrator (You can only see environments for which you're a system administrator.)

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance controls: trace and debug logging row
claims.claim: Website > Site settings in the management app is the path for the site setting used to enable trace and debug logging.
claims.quote: Using the Portal Management app, select Site settings under the Website section.
claims.fix: The pre-check's missing words are not a wrong path: the DevTools article links to the page that gives it. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/configure/configure-site-settings directly in ui.docs, retaining DevTools as the source for UserTrace/Debug=true.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls: trace and debug logging row
claims.claim: No automation equivalent is documented for managing the site-level trace and debug setting.
claims.quote: Support for download/upload of website configuration data to/from the local file system ... Supported tables ... adx_sitesetting
claims.fix: Replace the absence with documented PAC CLI configuration automation: download the site, update its UserTrace/Debug site setting, then upload it with pac pages upload --path <site-folder> --modelVersion <model-version>. Cite this page and explain that upload deploys edited configuration, not a dedicated logging toggle.

claims.where: controls[3].ui and controls[3].api; Governance controls: tenant-wide policy row
claims.claim: A tenant-wide policy specifically governing this analytics and server logging feature is not yet documented on either UI or API surfaces.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages Application Insights site analytics server logging tenant policy enable disable licensing; "Power Pages" "analytics" "tenant" "logging" policy. Read analytics, admin overview, DevTools and Websites API; no feature-wide policy found.

claims.where: controls[3].note; Governance controls: tenant-wide policy row
claims.claim: The roadmap entry describes a tenant-wide policy for analytics and server logging.
claims.quote: To configure site analytics, makers must open the setup workspace and add the analytics provider script to enable traffic analytics.
claims.fix: Replace the note with 'A tenant-wide policy for this feature is not yet documented as of November 2026; the roadmap describes maker configuration per site, not a tenant-wide policy.'

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn already documents Power Pages diagnostic logging.
claims.quote: To get the website error logs into your Azure Blob storage, you must enable diagnostic logging from the Power Platform admin center.

claims.claim: Learn documents the UserTrace/Debug site setting.
claims.quote: Add or update the Site Setting with the name UserTrace/Debug. ... Set the value to true.

claims.claim: The Power Pages DevTools extension displays server-side error messages.
claims.quote: It offers features such as displaying Liquid tracing message and server-side error messages.

claims.claim: Telemetry logs may retain IP addresses, creating a privacy risk.
claims.quote: By default, IP addresses are temporarily collected but not stored. ... To enable IP collection and storage, the DisableIpMasking property of the Application Insights component must be set to true.
claims.fix: Cite this page and qualify the risk: Application Insights masks stored IP addresses by default; retaining them requires an override. Keep the new feature's exact server/access-log fields explicitly unconfirmed rather than implying a published field schema.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Monitoring telemetry can contain request details that need protecting.
claims.quote: Request telemetry represents information related to incoming HTTP requests to your application.
claims.fix: Cite the Application Insights telemetry data model and present this as a general telemetry risk, not confirmation of the planned Power Pages server/access-log field schema.

claims.claim: Azure roles govern access to the Application Insights resource and its data.
claims.quote: View diagnostic settings, autoscale settings, and Application Insights data ... Monitoring Reader ... Yes ... Monitoring Contributor ... Yes
claims.fix: Add this Azure Monitor roles page to sources and cite it for Application Insights access control.

claims.claim: Existing site diagnostic logging writes application errors to an Azure Blob storage account owned by the customer.
claims.quote: To access the logs, configure your website to send all application errors to an Azure Blob storage account that you own.

claims.claim: The customer pays Azure storage charges for the account holding diagnostic logs.
claims.quote: Calculate your storage costs by multiplying the size of your data in GB by the storage price of the chosen access tier.
claims.fix: Add this Azure Blob Storage cost source; distinguish Blob storage charges from the separate Application Insights ingestion meter.

claims.claim: Retention configuration controls how long diagnostic log blobs are retained.
claims.quote: Select retention period: Duration to keep the portal error logs in blob storage. The error logs are deleted after the selected duration.
claims.fix: Replace the vague 'Azure retention policy' wording with the documented 'Select retention period' setting in Enable diagnostic logging or Update diagnostic logging configuration. Explain that it manages retained storage, not the Application Insights ingestion meter.

claims.claim: Everything documented in the controls section is per site.
claims.quote: controls[1]: scope: "tenant"; "Site traffic analytics". Closing paragraph: "Everything documented is per site and portal-driven."
claims.fix: Replace with 'Diagnostic logging and trace settings are site-specific; the admin analytics dashboard covers websites across the tenant, filtered by environment and site.'

claims.claim: All documented configuration is portal-driven rather than automatable.
claims.quote: With this feature, the Microsoft Power Platform CLI enables CI/CD (Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment) of a Power Pages site configuration.
claims.fix: Remove 'Everything documented is ... portal-driven.' State that management-app site settings can also be deployed with PAC CLI, while the diagnostic Blob logging enablement has no documented dedicated API equivalent found in this check.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents Power Pages activity logs in Microsoft Purview.
claims.quote: You can view many Microsoft Power Pages activities in Microsoft Purview, such as environment lifecycle operations, property and setting changes, groups and rules settings, licensing, lockbox operations, data policies, and admin actions.

claims.claim: Viewing Power Pages administrative activity logs in Purview needs no separate site setting.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Pages" "activity logs" "site setting" auditing. Opened activity-logs-power-pages and read its prerequisites; they name licensing, permissions, environment auditing and Purview auditing, not a site setting.
claims.fix: Keep the narrow no-site-setting statement, but immediately state that the linked article requires licensing and permissions review, auditing for the production environments, Purview auditing, and an Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs role. Do not imply no preparation is needed.

claims.claim: Microsoft's administration documentation identifies roles required for Power Pages administrative tasks.
claims.quote: The following table lists different administrative tasks for Power Pages, and the roles required to do that task.
claims.fix: Replace the admin-overview link with https://learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/admin/admin-roles and say it lists roles by administrative task; the overview merely links to that table.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Every technical control the checklist asks administrators to configure or review has a controls-table row.
claims.quote: Checklist: "Choose the Azure subscription, region and retention for Application Insights"; "Audit access to the Application Insights resource." The table has no Application Insights retention, spend-monitoring or access-control row.
claims.fix: Add rows for Application Insights retention/cost monitoring and Azure access control, with documented Azure paths or automation. Mark these as controls on the Azure telemetry destination, not confirmed tenant-wide Power Pages feature switches.

claims.claim: The prepare action rating fits a capability that requires a maker or administrator to add an analytics provider script.
claims.quote: action: "prepare"; "To configure site analytics, makers open the Set up workspace and add the analytics provider script."
claims.fix: Set action to review under the schema's optional-capability definition: the record describes explicit configuration and supplies no automatic change to existing sites or administrative deadline.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls: site traffic analytics row
claims.claim: An API or automation equivalent for the Power Pages site traffic analytics dashboard is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages site traffic analytics dashboard API daily weekly monthly active users. Read admin-center-analytics and the Power Platform Websites REST operations list; no equivalent Power Pages traffic analytics API found.

controlChecks.governs: Diagnostic logs for a site to Azure Blob storage
